To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have observed quasiparticle tunneling-induced excitations of the qubit and developed a model to explain this phenomenon.
the quasiparticle excitations of a superconducting phase qubit can be described by a simple stochastic model.
quasiparticle excitations of a superconducting charge-phase qubit can be described by a simple model of a two-level system coupled to an ensemble of quasiparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction between a superconducting quantum bit and a quasiparticle environment.
the development and characterization of quantum circuits for quantum information processing and quantum simulation.
the study of the interaction between a qubit and a non-equilibrium quasiclassical ensemble of quasiparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quasiparticles induce transitions in the qubit.
we have shown the existence of non-equilibrium excitations of the qubit by the quasiparticles.
the qubit is a mixed state with the excited state admixture of about 0.3%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to demonstrate a coherent control of a qubit state via a quasiparticle excitation and a coherent manipulation of the qubit state via an external microwave drive.
we have shown how to use a charge-phase qubit as a sensor for quasiparticles.
we have demonstrated that quasiparticle excitations are the main source of decoherence in the Al-based charge-phase qubit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a qubit can be in a mixed state due to the presence of quasiparticles, and the qubit can be excited even if it is in the ground state.
the qubit state is not a stationary one.
the qubit state can be monitored by a continuous measurement of the qubit's impedance.
